entries.title: Boundary partition law of a finite percolation gadget
entries.statement: For a finite undirected graph with labeled terminal vertices and a random open-edge configuration, its terminal partition puts two terminals in the same block exactly when an open path joins them inside the graph. The boundary-partition law is the probability distribution on these terminal partitions. When the graph attaches to an exterior only through those terminals, ordinary open-path connectivity in the union is determined by this partition and the exterior connectivity.
assumptions: The gadget meets the exterior only at the named terminal vertices.

entries.title: Finite independent-bond obstruction to an all-or-none selector
entries.statement: Let G be a finite undirected graph with k>=3 distinct terminals and mutually independent Bernoulli edges with probabilities in [0,1]. If the all-separated and all-connected terminal partitions both have positive probability, some strictly intermediate terminal partition has positive probability. Thus no such graph realizes a terminal law supported only on the two extreme partitions with both masses positive. If G has m optional edges whose probabilities lie in [epsilon,1-epsilon], 0<epsilon<=1/2, its partition law has total variation distance at least min(q,1-q,epsilon^m) from the selector assigning probability q to all-connected and 1-q to all-separated, for 0<q<1.
entries.proof_text: Delete forced-closed edges and contract forced-open connected components. Positive all-separated probability keeps the terminals distinct after contraction. Positive all-connected probability gives a possible-edge component containing every terminal. Choose a tree connecting them and prune nonterminal leaves. Deleting a tree edge splits its terminals into two nonempty blocks. Open the remaining tree edges and close all other optional edges. Every optional-edge assignment has positive probability, and this one has at least epsilon^m under the quantitative hypothesis. Its two terminal blocks form an intermediate partition because k>=3. Test the set of intermediate partitions to obtain the TV bound. If an extreme partition has zero probability instead, test that extreme event to get q or 1-q. The bound has no claimed uniformity as m grows.
assumptions: Finite undirected graph; k>=3 distinct labeled terminal vertices.
All Bernoulli edges are mutually independent.
The quantitative conclusion requires m optional edges and 0<epsilon<=1/2 bounding their probabilities away from zero and one.

entries.title: Exact finite replacement identity and exterior sensitivity bound
entries.statement: For finite coordinate state spaces S_i, product probability laws mu=product_i mu_i and nu=product_i nu_i, and F:product_i S_i->[0,1], define H_i as the independent exterior law using nu_j for j<i and mu_j for j>i. Then E_nu F-E_mu F equals sum_i E_H_i[sum_s (nu_i(s)-mu_i(s)) F(s,X_-i)]. If osc_i is the range of the local values of F over supp(mu_i) union supp(nu_i), the absolute expectation difference is at most sum_i TV(mu_i,nu_i) E_H_i osc_i. For an indicator F, osc_i is the indicator of exterior sensitivity to an admissible local state change. Sensitivity events for different i need not be independent.
entries.proof_text: Telescope the N+1 product laws whose first j coordinates use nu and whose remaining coordinates use mu. Adjacent laws have the same exterior H_i. Independence of the coordinate being replaced gives the conditional signed sum. The local signed measure nu_i-mu_i has total mass zero and positive mass TV(mu_i,nu_i). Subtract the minimum local value of F and bound the signed sum in absolute value by TV times the local oscillation. Average over H_i and use the triangle inequality. No multiplication of sensitivity probabilities is used.
assumptions: Finitely many finite coordinate state spaces.
Endpoint and hybrid laws are products on the same state spaces.

entries.title: Matched pair probabilities can change an exterior crossing
entries.statement: Let S be a fair all-or-none selector on three terminals a,b,c, and let T be a three-arm star whose arms are mutually independent Bernoulli(1/sqrt(2)). Every pair connection probability is 1/2 in both S and T. Add identical deterministic exterior wiring joining a to c, and ask whether b is connected to that wired pair. The crossing probability is 1/2 for S and 1-1/(2sqrt(2)) for T, differing by (2-sqrt(2))/4>0. Equal terminal-pair marginals therefore do not suffice for an exact gadget transfer in arbitrary exterior connectivity events.
entries.proof_text: With s=1/sqrt(2), a star pair is connected with probability s^2=1/2 and all three terminals are connected with probability s^3=1/(2sqrt(2)). The two events a~b and c~b have triple connection as their intersection. Inclusion-exclusion gives the wired crossing probability 2s^2-s^3. For the selector, both pair events occur exactly when its one fair hyperedge is open. The same deterministic exterior has been used in both cases. This is a finite replacement counterexample, not a refutation of asymptotic conformal invariance.
assumptions: The star arms are mutually independent with probability 1/sqrt(2).
The selector is one Bernoulli(1/2) hyperedge.
Exterior wiring a~c is deterministic and crossing means b connected to a or c.

entries.title: Unproved signed replacement gap for C0017
entries.statement: DRAFT OPEN PROOF OBLIGATION, not a theorem: for critical square-lattice bond percolation at p=1/2, this route has not constructed and controlled a comparison with critical triangular-lattice site percolation. It needs the actual endpoint laws and a proof that the total signed macroscopic crossing defect tends to zero, including boundary and exploration-conditioning controls. Exact finite independent-bond selectors with at least three terminals are obstructed, and equality of terminal-pair marginals cannot replace equality of boundary-partition laws. Even a crossing comparison would require further justification for interface tightness and SLE(6) identification. Current openness of C0017 is UNKNOWN in the bounded 2026-10-10 check because target-proof preprints exist but have not been audited here.
assumptions: Target concerns actual square-bond p=1/2 laws, not transformed or conditioned substitutes.
A mesh-dependent comparison and its limiting estimate remain unproved.

relations.rationale: The lemma's 'all-separated and all-connected terminal partitions' use the definition 'two terminals in the same block exactly when an open path joins them'.
The counterexample's 'Equal terminal-pair marginals' concerns the definition's full 'probability distribution on these terminal partitions'; these are different data.

The gap's 'Exact finite independent-bond selectors with at least three terminals are obstructed' is supported by the lemma's 'no such graph realizes a terminal law supported only on the two extreme partitions'.

The gap requires 'total signed macroscopic crossing defect tends to zero'; the identity gives the exact finite 'sum_i E_H_i[sum_s (nu_i(s)-mu_i(s)) F(s,X_-i)]' to control when a product comparison exists.
The gap's 'equality of terminal-pair marginals cannot replace equality of boundary-partition laws' is witnessed by the lemma's positive wired-crossing difference '(2-sqrt(2))/4'.
